claim: of neurons sit within 50 µm of a blood vessel
method: 10,441 neuron cell-body centres (somas.csv, away from the sample edges) to the nearest vertex of the finest blood-vessel meshes (1,477 segments). Median 22.9 µm; max 141 µm.
caveat: Distance to mesh vertices (spacing ~1.6 µm); the vessel segmentation may miss some capillaries, so true distances may be shorter. One ~1 mm³ sample of human temporal cortex.

claim: oligodendrocytes outnumber neurons in this human cortex sample
method: Cell types in H01 somas.csv; matches the paper's Table S5 exactly.
caveat: Driven by the white matter in the sample: in the grey-matter layers alone neurons outnumber oligodendrocytes (15,005 vs 9,350).

claim: of the cells in the sample's white matter are oligodendrocytes
method: 10,110 of 13,063 white-matter cells in somas.csv (half of all oligodendrocytes in the sample sit there). Script: github.com/shoo99/kbrain-map-numbers/blob/main/scripts/white-matter-oligodendrocytes.py
caveat: Layer labels are the dataset's own.

claim: synapses in just over one cubic millimetre of human cortex
method: Paper's automated count: 149,871,669 synapses in the volume.
caveat: Automated detection; the paper reports missed and false detections.

claim: inputs within 20 µm of one pyramidal neuron's cell body are inhibitory
method: All input synapses of cell 6644185383 in both public synapse releases; within 20 µm of the soma centre: 97.7% (20210601) and 96.5% (20210729, the release that matches the paper).
caveat: One cell. Labels partly depend on whether a synapse sits on a spine.

claim: across: a flat, whorled axon coiled on a neuron's cell body
method: Finest public meshes of the gallery's 'axon_whorl' (97 segments); disc ≈6 × 7 µm, ~1.6 µm thick; checked against the raw electron-microscopy images.
caveat: Automated segmentation; which pieces form the axon was chosen by the H01 team's gallery.

claim: of a glial cell's surface pressed against a neuron's cell body
method: Finest meshes of the gallery's 'parasitic_glial' cells: glial surface within 0.25 µm of the neuron (8% of the glial surface; ~5% of the neuron's cell-body surface).
caveat: One pair of cells; the glial cell is labelled microglia/OPC.

claim: fruit-fly neurons (about 1 in 7) are wired into the nerve cord
method: Superclass tags in the Janelia Male CNS segment properties (nerve-cord classes + ascending neurons). Independent check: MANC ~23,500 incl. 1,328 descending → ~22,200.
caveat: Only neurons with a superclass tag counted.

claim: predicted dopamine neurons in a complete fruit-fly connectome
method: Neurotransmitter predictions of named cell types; all 390 are named neurons, together making 803,309 output synapses.
caveat: Transmitter identity is predicted from EM, not measured chemically.

claim: named histamine neurons outside the fly's visual system
method: Connectome transmitter predictions, outside the optic lobes.
caveat: Predicted, not measured chemically.

claim: of the cells are neurons in layer 1, the cortex's top layer, versus layer 2 just below
method: Cells by the dataset's layer labels (somas.csv): layer 1 — 827 neurons of 4,595 cells (586 interneurons, 72 pyramidal); layer 2 — 4,656 of 6,651. Script: github.com/shoo99/kbrain-map-numbers/blob/main/scripts/layer1-few-neurons.py
caveat: Layer labels are the dataset's own; one sample. Layer 1 is mostly wiring: pyramidal-cell branch tips meeting long-range inputs (Schuman et al. 2021).

claim: of the cells in layer 1 are astrocytes — the most common cell in the cortex's top layer
method: Cells by the dataset's layer labels (somas.csv): layer 1 — 1,688 astrocytes of 4,595 cells; 1,688 of the sample's 5,474 astrocytes (30.8%) sit in layer 1. Consistent with the paper's Table S4 (astrocyte volume fraction 21.6% in layer 1 vs 14–15% in layers 2–6). Script: github.com/shoo99/kbrain-map-numbers/blob/main/scripts/layer1-astrocytes.py
caveat: One sample; layer labels are the dataset's own. The map does not tell astrocyte subtypes apart (e.g. primate-specific interlaminar astrocytes, Oberheim et al. 2009).

claim: of the neurons in this human cortex sample are inhibitory — almost 1 in 3, versus about 12% in a mouse cortex map
method: Neurons by the dataset's own cell-type labels (somas.csv): 4,688 interneurons of 15,219 classified neurons (pyramidal 8,803, spiny atypical 1,535, spiny stellate 193, interneuron 4,688). Mouse: MICrONS cell table (mouse visual cortex), 9,017 inhibitory of 75,405 classified neurons = 12.0%. Loomba et al. 2022 (Science) report a 2.5-fold larger interneuron pool in human than mouse cortex. Script: github.com/shoo99/kbrain-map-numbers/blob/main/scripts/inhibitory-third.py
caveat: One human sample (temporal cortex, epilepsy surgery). 868 unclassified neurons left out (with them: 29.1%). The share varies by layer (L2–3 about 35–37%, L6 12%). Human and mouse maps cover different brain areas and were classified by different methods.

claim: microglia and OPCs in every cortical layer — the one cell class spread evenly, varying only about 10% from layer 1 to layer 6
method: Paper Table S6 (cells per mm³ by layer, corrected for 28% compression): microglia/OPC 6,329 / 6,490 / 6,519 / 5,922 / 5,854 / 6,004 in layers 1–6 (max/min 1.11). Neurons vary 6.4-fold across the same layers (5,272 to 33,745), oligodendrocytes 5.1-fold, astrocytes 3.4-fold.
caveat: The dataset counts microglia and OPCs as one class. The reason given (cells keep their distance; a neighbour moves in when one is lost) was shown for OPCs in adult mice (Hughes et al. 2013), not for microglia or for human tissue. One sample.

claim: of the mapped white-matter volume is the inside of myelinated axons (sheaths not counted) — versus only 1.0% in layer 1, the cortex's top layer
method: Paper Table S4 (volume occupancy by layer): myelinated axon 1.0 / 0.8 / 2.5 / 4.8 / 5.6 / 7.7 / 31.5% in layers 1–6 and white matter. The video pairs two raw electron-microscope tiles (layer 1 and white matter) from the same sample.
caveat: One sample (human temporal cortex, epilepsy surgery). The paper's class is myelinated axons excluding their myelin sheaths, and the shares are of the segmented tissue: 36% of voxels (myelin sheaths among them) were not segmented. So 31.5% is not the share of every cubic micrometre of white matter. These are the paper's values, not our own count.

claim: of the mapped tissue in every cortical layer is wire (axons and dendrites); cell bodies take up about 10%
method: Paper Table S4 (volume occupancy by layer, % of segmented tissue). Wire = axon + dendrite + myelinated axon: 74.1 / 73.1 / 74.3 / 70.4 / 72.7 / 73.1% in layers 1–6. Cell bodies: 2.1 / 10.6 / 9.6 / 12.9 / 11.8 / 11.1%. Axons alone 40.0–44.4%, dendrites 23.1–32.3%. Sums are ours.
caveat: Shares are of the tissue the paper could classify: 36% of voxels, including myelin sheaths, were not segmented, so these are not shares of every cubic micrometre. One sample (human temporal cortex, epilepsy surgery). The ~60% optimum is a theory (Chklovskii et al. 2002), not measured in human tissue.

claim: neurons in layer 2, the most crowded layer of this human cortex sample; layer 4 is next (~29,000), layer 1 has ~5,000
method: Paper Table S6 (cells per mm³ by layer, corrected for 28% compression). Neurons = spiny + interneurons + unclassified: L1 5,272 · L2 33,745 · L3 14,314 · L4 29,463 · L5 14,118 · L6 11,456 · white matter 4,174. Layers II and IV are the classical external and internal granular layers.
caveat: One sample (human temporal cortex, epilepsy surgery). Layer borders are the H01 team's, drawn from cell positions and sizes. Densities differ between cortical areas.

claim: of synapses in this human cortex sample are inhibitory ("stop") once the automated count is corrected; the raw count said 26%
method: Supplementary methods: the automated pipeline classified 111,272,315 synapses as excitatory and 38,599,354 as inhibitory (inhibitory 25.75% of the raw count; our calculation). People annotated 5,554 true synapses on 42 axons (25 excitatory, 17 inhibitory; Table S3): the detector missed 11% of excitatory and 35% of inhibitory synapses, with false discovery rates of 3.2% and 2.7%. Corrected for missed, false and misclassified synapses, the main text estimates 111.6 M excitatory (61.2%) and 70.7 M inhibitory (38.8%) synapses.
caveat: The 38.8% is the paper's estimate; we could not reproduce it exactly from the published formula and global counts (it was probably applied per 10 µm cube), and a global plug-in gives about 37%. Error rates come from 42 axons. One sample (human temporal cortex, epilepsy surgery).

claim: of the neurons in this human cortex sample are pyramidal cells (8,803 of 16,087), each classified by people
method: Paper, Table S5 (manual counts of all cells): pyramidal 8,803; other excitatory (spiny 1,535, spiny stellate 193); interneurons 4,688; unclassified neurons 868; all neurons 16,087. 8,803 / 16,087 = 54.7% (our division). The public somas.csv gives the same counts. Cell types were assigned by hand from the EM images and 3D shapes (supplementary methods).
caveat: One sample (human temporal cortex, epilepsy surgery). "Extrapyramidal" is not a cell type; it names motor pathways outside the pyramidal (corticospinal) tract.

claim: cells in this human cortex sample belongs to the blood vessels (about 8,000 of 57,000, counted by hand)
method: Paper, Table S5 (manual counts of all cells): all blood-vessel-related cells 8,136 of 57,216 cells = 14.2% (our division). Sub-rows: endothelial cells 4,604, pericytes 3,549, circulating immune cells 46, blood-vessel cells in the main cell list 285.
caveat: The sub-rows do not add up exactly to 8,136, and the main text gives about 8,100 of 57,180 cells, so we round to about 8,000 and 1 in 7. One sample (human temporal cortex, epilepsy surgery).

claim: of the neurons in this human temporal cortex sample are spiny stellate ("star") cells: 193 of 16,087
method: Paper, Table S5 (manual counts of all cells): spiny stellate 193 of 16,087 neurons = 1.2% (our division). The public somas.csv gives the same counts. Cell types were assigned by hand from EM appearance and 3D shape (supplementary methods).
caveat: One sample, from the anterior middle temporal gyrus (association cortex, epilepsy surgery). Spiny stellate cells are typical of layer 4 in primary sensory areas, so a low count here is expected; it says nothing about visual or touch cortex. The paper's layers are data-driven, so we do not report where in the layers these cells sit.

claim: slices, about 34 nanometres thick on average, were cut from this speck of human cortex and photographed; the imaging took 326 days
method: Supplementary methods: "In total, 5019 sections were cut, ranging in thickness between 30 and 80nm, with 92.5% between 30 and 33nm"; average thickness as cut 33.9 nm (Table S10). Main text: total imaging time 326 days; the aligned image volume is about 1.4 petabytes (1.8 PB of raw tiles).
caveat: Some sections were cut double-thick and are shown twice in the online viewer, which therefore has 5,293 digital sections. One sample (a 170 µm thick slab of human temporal cortex, epilepsy surgery).

claim: neurons to glia in layer 2 of this human cortex sample, the one layer where neurons outnumber glia (overall, glia win about 2 to 1)
method: Paper, Table S6 (cells per mm³, compression-corrected). Layer 2: neurons (spiny 21,467 + interneurons 11,655 + unclassified 623) = 33,745; glia (astrocytes 3,592 + oligodendrocytes 3,872 + microglia/OPC 6,490) = 13,954; ratio ours. White matter: glia 65,552 vs neurons 4,174, about 16 to 1. Overall: Table S5, 32,315 glia vs 16,087 neurons. Recounting somas.csv gives 0.42 glia per neuron in layer 2 and 18.8 in white matter.
caveat: One sample (human temporal cortex, epilepsy surgery). The paper's layers are data-driven clusters. The paper links myelin to oligodendrocyte density (both lowest in layer 2); it does not test why layer 2 has fewer glia.

claim: synapses for every astrocyte in this human cortex sample, on average (about 150 million synapses, 5,474 astrocytes)
method: Paper abstract: ~150 million synapses. Table S5: 5,474 astrocytes (counted by hand). 150,000,000 / 5,474 ≈ 27,400 (our division).
caveat: An average from two sample totals, not a measured count of the synapses each astrocyte touches. The synapse total comes from automated detection. One sample (human temporal cortex, epilepsy surgery).

claim: glia per neuron in human cortex grey matter (H01) vs mouse visual cortex (MICrONS): humans have about five times more glia for each neuron
method: Mouse: MICrONS public cell table aibs_cell_info (materialization v1300; column names from aibs_cell_info_header.csv). Neurons = broad_type excitatory 66,388 + inhibitory 9,017 = 75,405. Glia = broad_type nonneuron with cell_type astrocyte 7,851 + oligo 7,035 + microglia 2,635 + OPC 1,663 = 19,184 (cell_type mostly from aibs_metamodel_celltypes_v661). 19,184 / 75,405 = 0.25 (ours). Human: H01 somas.csv, layers 1 to 6 only: glia (ASTROCYTE, OLIGO, MG_OPC, C_SHAPED) 19,238 / neurons (PYRAMIDAL, SPINY_ATYPICAL, SPINY_STELLATE, INTERNEURON, UNCLASSIFIED_NEURON) 15,005 = 1.28 (ours). Script: github.com/shoo99/kbrain-map-numbers/blob/main/scripts/glia-per-neuron-human-mouse.py
caveat: One sample per species, different cortical areas (human temporal association cortex vs mouse visual cortex). 46,739 mouse nuclei (32%) have no class; even if all were glia the mouse ratio would be 0.87, still below the human value. Cell types come from each project's own classification (manual in H01, mostly automated in MICrONS). Why the ratio differs: across species it rises as neurons get larger and less densely packed (Herculano-Houzel 2014, Glia 62:1377).

claim: of the neurons labelled inhibitory ("brake") in this mouse visual cortex sample are labelled basket cells, the type that grips other neurons around their cell bodies; most labels come from a model that reads the cell body and nucleus
method: MICrONS public cell table aibs_cell_info (materialization v1300; column names from aibs_cell_info_header.csv). 9,017 cells with broad_type inhibitory; 3,374 of them have cell_type BC = 37% (ours). Source of those 3,374 labels (cell_type_source): aibs_metamodel_celltypes_v661 3,283 (hierarchical classifier trained on features of the cell body and nucleus; Elabbady et al. 2025, Nature 640:478), allen_v1_column_types_slanted_ref 59 (typed by hand by Allen Institute anatomists), aibs_metamodel_celltypes_v661_corrections 32. The separate mtype label PTC (perisomatic targeting cells, roughly basket cells; Schneider-Mizell et al. 2025, Nature 640:448) gives 3,054 = 34%. Script: github.com/shoo99/kbrain-map-numbers/blob/main/scripts/mouse-basket-cells.py
caveat: Mostly model predictions; BC and PTC come from the same AIBS model family, so they are not independent checks. broad_type and cell_type come from different classifiers and disagree for some cells (933 cells with broad_type inhibitory carry an excitatory cell_type). One sample (mouse visual cortex). The human H01 data do not label inhibitory subtypes. Corrected 2026-11-15: an earlier version of this card called BC and PTC two independent methods and named the wrong source column.

claim: bigger: the typical neuron nucleus vs the typical microglia nucleus in this mouse visual cortex sample (about 280 vs 73 cubic microns)
method: MICrONS public cell table aibs_cell_info (materialization v1300; column names from aibs_cell_info_header.csv), column nuc_volume. Median 278 µm³ for 75,405 neurons (broad_type excitatory or inhibitory) vs 72.5 µm³ for 2,635 microglia (broad_type nonneuron, cell_type microglia) = 3.8× (ours). Hand-typed cells only (1,333 neurons from allen_v1_column_types_slanted_ref, 60 microglia from aibs_column_nonneuronal_ref): 288 vs 74 = 3.9×. Pericytes have the smallest median, 51 µm³ (2,780 cells). Units: the table does not state them; we measured the two nuclei in the shown EM section (minnie65, 16 nm pixels): neuron about 8 × 10 µm, microglia about 3.6 × 7.6 µm, consistent with µm³. Script: github.com/shoo99/kbrain-map-numbers/blob/main/scripts/mouse-nucleus-size.py
caveat: One sample (mouse visual cortex). Nucleus volumes come from the dataset's automatic nucleus detection; most cell types are model predictions. Medians hide wide ranges (neurons 10th to 90th percentile 223 to 362 µm³ for excitatory). Why (review, not measured here): nuclear size scales with cell size, not DNA content (Cantwell & Nurse 2019, Curr Genet 65:1281).
